Show Rate and Sales Pipeline Guide
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL FOR TESTS

Why we track every stage
Every stage of the pipeline converts into the next one. When revenue is low, one stage is usually the bottleneck. Fix that stage first.
The pipeline stages are: DM sent, reply, quality conversation, link sent, call booked, call showed, closed.

Benchmarks for each stage
Benchmark: DM reply rate should be at least 10 percent of DMs sent. Below 8 percent means the opener is the problem.
Benchmark: at least 40 percent of replies should turn into a quality conversation.
Benchmark: at least 50 percent of quality conversations should get the booking link.
Benchmark: at least 30 percent of people who get the link should book a call.
Benchmark: show rate should be at least 60 percent of booked calls. Under 50 percent is an emergency.
Benchmark: close rate should be at least 20 percent of calls that showed.
Benchmark: webinar registration rate should be at least 25 percent of landing page visitors.
Benchmark: webinar show rate should be at least 35 percent of registrants.
Benchmark: webinar close rate should be at least 5 percent of attendees.
Benchmark: cost per lead should stay under 15 dollars for a cold audience.
Benchmark: cost per acquisition should stay under 30 percent of the offer price.

How to raise the show rate
Send a confirmation message within five minutes of the booking.
Send three reminders: twenty-four hours before the call, two hours before the call, and ten minutes before the call.
Each reminder gives value. Share a short video or a question to think about. Never just say "don't forget".
Ask the lead to reply to confirm. A lead who replies is far more likely to show up.
Book calls within forty-eight hours. The longer the gap between booking and call, the lower the show rate.

What to do with a no-show
Message a no-show within fifteen minutes. Keep it kind and offer two new times.
Do not shame the lead. People miss calls for real reasons.
If they do not reply after two attempts, move them to the nurture list.

The pre-call brief
Before every call the closer reads a pre-call brief: the lead's goal, their current numbers, their main obstacle, and what they said in the DMs.
A closer who walks in without a brief sounds like a stranger. A closer with a brief sounds like a doctor who read the chart.
